turns.question: From Wakefield Cathedral to Yorkshire Sculpture Park tomorrow, by bus
turns.reply:
The 96 bus runs Monday–Sunday between Wakefield and Barnsley, with regular stops at Yorkshire Sculpture Park.
 Tomorrow is Monday 16 November, so the 96 will be running.

From Wakefield Cathedral, 
the city centre bus station (WF1 3AQ) is located just a 5-minute walk from the cathedral, and 
the 96 operates from stand 10 at Wakefield Bus Station.

turns.question: Plan a wheelchair-accessible free day out with children in Wakefield city centre
turns.reply:
Today is Sunday, so a few planned venues are closed, but there's plenty to do. Here's a wheelchair-accessible free day out:

Morning: Wakefield Museum

Wakefield Museum is free entry for all.
 
It's level access and fully wheelchair accessible throughout.
 
All areas are accessible for pushchairs and wheelchairs, with lots of hands-on elements including dress-up, a toy 1950s kitchen, and creative activities.
 
Blue Badge parking is at Merchant Gate car park, which has a short two-minute step-free route to the museum including a slight incline that wheelchairs and pushchairs can access.

The museum is open today until 4pm. Note that 
Create Café is opposite the museum entrance but open Tuesday to Thursday only, so that's not an option today.

Lunch: City centre cafe options

Since today is Sunday, your best verified accessible stops are 
Wakefield Library (accessible toilet, baby changing, wheelchair accessible)
 or explore the city-centre food options at WX Wakefield Exchange, which offers 
wheelchair-accessible facilities including accessible car parking, accessible toilets, and step-free access.

Afternoon: Outdoor free activity

Thornes Park has a play area with equipment for children of different abilities, including an inclusive swing seat, basket swing, wheelchair-accessible roundabout and low-level sensory panels.
 The park is free to visit, though 
the Wakefield freecitybus runs every 10–12 minutes and is fully accessible (carrying one wheelchair at a time).

Evening option (if you want to extend):

Light Up Wakefield runs until 9pm tonight and is free, family-friendly and wheelchair accessible with accessible parking, accessible toilets, Changing Places facility and step-free access.
 
The event hub is based at WX Wakefield Exchange.

All three main stops are verified as genuinely wheelchair accessible with proper facilities, not just assumed from the building type.
